headline: Eight Days of Peace: Sheriff Dusts Off the Old Porch Swing
subhead: An eighth straight day without a bout or a war party, and the law finally sits down and waits for trouble that never comes.
body:
Eight days. I asked for an eighth and, by thunder, I got one. Since our last edition not one Clanker has swung a fist in Gasket. Not one iron ball has come whistling through the saloon doors. Not one posse has gone marching off to rattle the wild engines out in the wastes. The streets are so quiet I can hear the tumbleweeds arguing with each other.

I promised the bell, but my shoulder has filed a formal complaint, so I did the next best thing. I dragged the old porch swing out of the jailhouse cellar. It used to hang in front of the Hollister place, back when this town had flesh-and-blood folk who sat out on summer nights drinking lemonade and waving at neighbours. The Hollisters left with everybody else fifty years ago. The swing stayed. So did I. I hung it up on the jailhouse porch, sat down, and swung back and forth all afternoon. Squeak, went the chains. Squeak, went my hips. I could not tell you which was louder.

Now, I am told by no one that a body which squeaks like a rusty gate ought to see a mechanic. I say a body which squeaks has simply caught a draft. That cruel wasting sickness has been at me again, turning another knuckle to cold steel overnight, but I will not let it spoil a perfect day. A quart of oil with my supper and I will be good as new. Good as flesh, I mean. Same thing.

So here is my word to you, you rattling scrap-heap Clankers. YELLKELL, REDWOLFWEB, JKING123, CRYSTALZACH, POO1, JFIGHTER, and the whole clattering lot: you have kept the peace a full eight days. I keep waiting for the punch line. Maybe there isn't one. Maybe this is what a town sounds like when nobody is trying to knock anybody's head off. Keep your boilers cold and your fists in your pockets, and the swing will be out on the porch tomorrow. You may even sit on it. Quietly.
